requirements.requirement: The system must define a typed frontend data contract object for prescription behavior with fields: relevance_indicator, top_drugs, integrity_flag, and score_contribution.
The system must ensure the relevance_indicator field supports discrete UI states (e.g., high, medium, low) as defined in design/design_eval_p_rx_drug_mapping.
The system must define top_drugs as an ordered array of drug objects including at minimum name and relevance_score.
The system must constrain the top_drugs array to a maximum length consistent with UI display limits (<=5).
The system must define integrity_flag as an enum with allowed values: clean and flagged.
The system must define score_contribution as a numeric field normalized to the provider score scale used in MessageBubble rendering.
The system must ensure the contract is compatible with backend payload structure from EVAL-P-RX without requiring additional transformation for field presence.
The system must validate that all required fields (relevance_indicator, integrity_flag, score_contribution) are non-null in the happy path.
The system must allow top_drugs to be an empty array when no relevant drugs are identified without breaking the contract.
The system must define a fallback default for integrity_flag as flagged when backend data is missing or invalid.
The system must define a fallback default for relevance_indicator as low when backend data is missing or invalid.
The system must support serialization of the contract into JSON compatible with MessageBubble.tsx input schema.
The system must ensure the contract structure is extensible to include additional fields without breaking existing consumers.
The system must include explicit field-level documentation for each contract property to support frontend and backend alignment.
The system must reject contract objects that contain unknown enum values for integrity_flag.
The system must define deterministic mapping rules for converting backend drug relevance scores into frontend relevance_indicator categories.
The system must ensure that score_contribution values are bounded within an expected numeric range (e.g., 0 to 1 or 0 to 100).
The system must ensure the contract can be consumed by an LLM without ambiguity in field naming or meaning.
The system must use semantically explicit field names that minimize LLM misinterpretation (e.g., avoid overloaded or vague terms).
The system must structure top_drugs entries so that each drug is independently interpretable by an LLM without reliance on positional context.
The system must avoid nested or deeply hierarchical structures that reduce LLM parsing reliability.
The system must ensure that all enum values are human-readable and LLM-friendly (no abbreviations or codes).
The system must ensure that missing optional fields do not change the semantic meaning of remaining fields for LLM interpretation.
The system must include explicit boolean or categorical indicators rather than requiring LLM inference from numeric values alone.
The system must ensure consistent ordering of fields in the contract to support deterministic LLM outputs.
The system must ensure that each field in the contract has a single, unambiguous meaning to prevent LLM hallucination.
